paper.title: Lookahead identification in adversarial bandits: accuracy and memory bounds

unmapped: Lookahead identification: learner chooses a stopping time t0 and window w and commits to an arm whose average reward over the future window [t0, t0+w] is epsilon-optimal
settings.definition_quote: An algorithm for lookahead BAI outputs a window size $w \in [T]$, a stopping time $t_0 \le T-w$, and an arm $\hat{i}\in[K]$, such that it achieves $\epsilon$-best expected cumulative gain over the window

unmapped: Lookahead identification objective (future window chosen by learner)
settings.definition_quote: We will prove a stronger claim, by considering any algorithm that may {\it fully observe} the values of {\it both} arms

settings.name_in_paper: Lookahead BAI memory lower bound (full observation)
unmapped: Bounded memory (bits) is the measured resource
Window w > T/c with randomized t0 declared ahead of the run
settings.definition_quote: consider any algorithm $\mathcal A$ which solves the lookahead best-arm identification task using any $w > w_0$ and a randomized $t_0$ declared ahead of the run

settings.name_in_paper: Lookahead BAI for locally sparse bandits
unmapped: Instance is locally phi-sparse (||n||_2^2/n_1^2 <= phi on every window of size w >= sqrt(T))
Learner knows the sparsity parameter phi
settings.definition_quote: We say that $X$ is a \emph{locally} $\phi$-\emph{sparse} bandit instance with window size $w \in [T]$, if for every contiguous set of indices $I \subset [T]$ of size $w$, then $Y|_{I}$ the restriction of $X$ to the columns in $I$, is  $\phi$-\emph{sparse}.

settings.name_in_paper: Regret minimization for bandits with bounded memory
settings.definition_quote: we study the classical regret minimization objective under memory constraints

conditions: oblivious adversary, X in [0,1]^{K x T}

source.label: thm:bandit_bai
source.quote: Let $K, T \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $K = \tilde{O}({{T^{1/4}}})$. For any bandit instance $X \in [0,1]^{K \times T}$, Algorithm \ref{alg:bandit_bai} returns $t_0$, window size $w = \Omega(\sqrt{T})$, and arm $\hat{i}$ such that, E[...] \le \frac{20}{\sqrt{{\log(T)}}}

results.notes: Bound on expected lookahead error (average reward gap over chosen future window), not regret. Proof ends with 10/sqrt(log T) for epsilon and 2*epsilon total, consistent with 20.

source.label: thm:bandit_bai_err_lb
source.quote: Let $K=2$ and $T = 2^M$ for $M \in \mathbb{N}$. Then, for any algorithm for the lookahead BAI task, there exists an instance $X \in [0,1]^{K \times T}$ for which the algorithm must incur an expected error of at least $1/{(8\log(T))}$.

results.notes: Proof gives 1/(8M) with M = log2 T; holds even for fully-observing algorithms. Log base ambiguous.

conditions: window w > T/c for a constant c > 1
randomized t0 declared ahead of the run
algorithm outputs epsilon-best arm with constant probability

source.label: thm:bandit_bai_memory_lb
source.quote: Let $K,T\in\mathbb{N}$ and fix a constant $c>1$ with $T|c$. Let $w_0 =T/c$ and consider any algorithm $\mathcal A$ which solves the lookahead best-arm identification task using any $w > w_0$ and a randomized $t_0$ declared ahead of the run, and outputs the $\epsilon$-best arm with constant probability and, for $\epsilon \in (1/10, 1/5)$. Then $\mathcal A$ must use $\Omega(K)$ bits of memory.

results.notes: Lower bound on memory (bits), not on error. Via reduction from set disjointness; holds even with full observation.

conditions: instance locally phi-sparse for all w >= sqrt(T)

source.label: thm:sparse_bai
source.quote: Let $K, T \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $K = \tilde{O}({{T^{1/4}}})$, and let $\delta >0$. Set $\epsilon' = 2/\sqrt{\log(T)}$, $\delta' = \delta\epsilon'$. For any bandit instance $X \in [0,1]^{K \times T}$ that is locally $\phi$-sparse for all $w \ge \sqrt{T}$, with probability at least $1-\delta$ we have that Algorithm \ref{alg:sparse_bandit_bai} uses at most $\sigma = \tilde{O}(\phi)$ bits of memory, and returns ... \le \frac{10}{\sqrt{{\log(T)}}}.

results.notes: Statement mixes 'with probability 1-delta' with an expectation bound; the proof actually derives 100/sqrt(log T), inconsistent with stated 10. Recorded as stated.

symbols.phi: local sparsity parameter of the instance

conditions: instance locally phi-sparse for all w >= sqrt(T)

source.label: thm:sparse_bai
source.quote: with probability at least $1-\delta$ we have that Algorithm \ref{alg:sparse_bandit_bai} uses  at most $\sigma = \tilde{O}(\phi)$ bits of memory

results.notes: Memory bound in bits; O~ hides polylog factors in T and 1/delta.

tuning: base learner: Algorithm 8 of Peng & Rubinstein (2023)

source.label: thm:bm_mab
source.quote: For sufficiently large $K$ and $T$, there exists an algorithm that achieves regret at most $\tilde O(T^{2/3}K^{1/3})$ in the bandit setting with probability at least $1-2/(KT)^{O(1)}$, using at most $\sigma=O(\text{poly-log}(KT))$ bits of memory.

results.notes: Probability 1-2/(KT)^{O(1)}; memory polylog(KT) bits. Proof also gives the same bound in expectation.
